blocker.mechanism: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs returns 302 to a SIGNED Azure Blob Storage URL (productionresultssa4.blob.core.windows.net). urllib's default redirect handler re-sends the Authorization: Bearer header to that host. Azure rejects a signed request that also carries an Authorization header, returning HTTP 401 'Server failed to authenticate the request. Please refer to the information in the www-authenticate header'. transport.py maps any 401 to AuthenticationError, so a redirect bug is reported as a GitHub credential failure.
proof: Same token, same endpoint, same session: the only variable is whether Authorization survives the cross-host redirect.
blocker.environment_independent: GitHub always redirects job logs to blob storage, so this fails wherever the resolver runs, including CI. It is not specific to this sandbox.
blocker.fix: Strip the Authorization header when a redirect crosses to a different host (what requests and curl do by default). A ~6-line HTTPRedirectHandler subclass in transport.py.

resolver_producer_stage_1.note: Real resolver code projected the real Core-driven SDK FindingBundle onto l9.sdk-knowledge-document/v1. This is the resolver-side input build-feedback-event needs.  Also proven: with the redirect defect worked around, acquire-github-run completes and emits a real l9.evidence-bundle/v1 from a real failed CI run.

intelligence_consumer_accepts_real_produ.note: This is the SDK -> Intelligence ingestion path, NOT the resolver -> Intelligence seam. It proves Intelligence's real ingestion code accepts real producer output; it is explicitly NOT a substitute for the blocked resolver feedback path.

idempotency.evidence: Re-ingesting the identical bundle returned status=duplicate with the SAME record_id (cr_9584d55d...) and ledger_sequence=2. verify-store reports status=valid, ledger_entries=2, record_count=1, duplicates=1 - the append-only ledger recorded the delivery without creating a second corpus record.

pseudonymisation_enforced.evidence: Intelligence refused to ingest until L9_INTELLIGENCE_PSEUDONYM_KEY and L9_INTELLIGENCE_PATH_KEY were both set, stating the corpus would otherwise partition by producer. Repository identity is pseudonymised, never stored raw.

test_scoped_config.note: Non-secret test-scoped keys for a throwaway corpus under artifacts/. Not credentials.

failure.summary: Seam blocked by a reproducible cross-host redirect auth-forwarding defect in l9-ci-debt-resolver's GitHub transport, previously and incorrectly attributed to missing credentials.

retraction.what_was_wrong: An earlier revision of this receipt classified the blocker as 'credentials - this surface holds no GitHub credential the resolver's transport can use' and set status=partial. That was WRONG.
retraction.how_it_was_disproved: GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN are present and WORK: a direct REST call and a plain urllib.request.urlopen with that token both return HTTP 200 against the same Actions endpoints the resolver uses.
retraction.corrected_status: fail - a reproducible defect in l9-ci-debt-resolver, not an environment limit.

diagnostic_confirmation.method: Ran the resolver's REAL acquisition with a runtime-only opener that strips Authorization on cross-host redirect. No repository source was modified.
diagnostic_confirmation.result: pass - the redirect bug is the SOLE blocker of log acquisition.

second_blocker.error: SDK snapshot does not match repository revision
second_blocker.assessment: CORRECT fail-closed behaviour, not a defect. The evidence bundle is an l9-ci-core run while the available SDK knowledge was built from an l9-pr-repair scan. Completing the seam needs a failed CI run AND an SDK bundle at the SAME revision. No failed run exists at any revision checked out here (origin/main 4c842cb has none, and PR #150's runs are all green), and switching a shared clone to the failing run's branch is forbidden.
second_blocker.classification: test-data alignment, not a code defect
